_doc: Provider x capability x helm-level support matrix. Companion to top-level-runtime-contract.md §4. Consumed by conformance-matrix.js (gate 'support-matrix').
_encoding_note: Each row's capabilities map gives, per capability, the set of helm-levels (0-3) at which that capability is declared PROVEN supported, plus an evidence_ref. Level 3 (MC Master Console, 'long-term target') is NOT built for ANY helm — no row's supported_levels includes 3. A row's status is one of 'supported', 'down' or 'not-verified' (conformance-matrix.js refuses any other value at load); 'down' and 'not-verified' are both unavailable statuses and every gate reads them identically (a required row in either resolves BLOCKED).

helm_levels.0: chat-only (plan/review only, cannot safely operate MC alone)
helm_levels.1: file-aware (reads repo, produces patches; no command execution)
helm_levels.3: MC Master Console (provider-neutral top-level UI/API; long-term target, not yet built for any helm)

agy-antigravity.note: CONTRACTED (panel-3lab is the binding 1.0 profile; agy is in-scope). The row ships status:not-verified / proven:false: the shipped matrix records no attested agy serve, and every gate reads not-verified exactly like down — a not-verified REQUIRED lane resolves BLOCKED, never a silent pass (see durable_rule below). panel-2family gates while the agy lane is unavailable; panel-3lab is the binding exit once it is. Attestation (evaluateAttestation) requires positive served-model proof; the lane is verified only when one genuine authenticated serve of the contracted model is attested.

kernel_scope.in: helm x capability x helm-level support contract (this file) + the model x channel Addendum A seed. Both are SEED data, positively fixture-covered (gate 'support-matrix').
kernel_scope.out: per-request routing POLICY; the full panel-3lab BINDING gate; product-pack/webapp/founder-panel provider gates (lastmile, never kernel scope).

durable_rule: A lane resolved DOWN or NOT-VERIFIED is reflected in EVERY artifact that assumed it UP. conformance-matrix.js reads the 'status' field directly (not a cached/echoed liveness claim) so a false-green agy seed cannot propagate into the panel lane contract — a config-intent echo is NOT liveness.
write_durable_state_note: Disambiguation: a row's 'write-durable-state' capability describes an UNTRUSTED-PROPOSAL capability -- a provider writing to an isolated worktree it does not control the integration of, or proposing a change via the trusted dispatch bridge (scripts/dispatch-claude.js / scripts/dispatch-agent.js). It does NOT mean, and must never be read as, a grant of CORE-2's protected-mutation or integration-to-main powers (top-level-runtime-contract.md §1/§4) -- those two powers stay SOLELY with the provider-independent trusted layer regardless of any row's supported_levels here. See each row's write-durable-state.evidence_ref for the per-provider restatement.
durable_state_mutation_capabilities_note: The disambiguation above applies to EVERY capability in this matrix that mutates durable company state, not only 'write-durable-state'. 'update-tracker' is the other one in this matrix -- top-level-runtime-contract.md §1 names trackers explicitly among the four CORE-2 protected-mutation targets ('trackers, ledgers, registries'), so a row's update-tracker capability is under the exact same disambiguation: PROPOSAL via an isolated worktree or the trusted dispatch bridge, never direct protected mutation of the integrated/main TRACKER.md. See each row's update-tracker.evidence_ref for the per-provider restatement. Any FUTURE capability added to this matrix that mutates durable company state must receive the same per-capability evidence_ref treatment -- do not leave a sibling capability unscoped.
